subject: dplyr joins: Inconsitent behavior when matching on strings and factors

messages.author: 746a110d20a6f112
messages.subject: dplyr joins: Inconsitent behavior when matching on strings and factors
parts:
Hi All-

I recently discovered (through trial and error) that the '_join' functions will not match if one of the variables is a string and the other is a factor, but also does not produce an error message telling the user, and (at least with small datasets) will return the first match but not others.

It seems like the issue was discussed and (resolved) here: https://github.com/hadley/dplyr/issues/228.  I could be misreading it but seems as though the consensus was that all strings (factor otherwise) should be converted to charaters to avoid this issue.

A reproducible example is available here (http://rpubs.com/frank_davenport/22116 ) and included below. Can someone tell me if this is a bug or by design? If it is by design, it might help in future versions to at least have a warning message stating that matches between strings and factors will not work. Or maybe I am completely missing something?

My personal preference is to have _join behave the same as merge() where strings/factors are converted and matched automatically.

Thanks again to Hadley et al. for all the great work, and as always apologies if this already addressed elsewhere.

library(dplyr)
##
## Attaching package: 'dplyr'
##
## The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
##
##     filter, lag
##
## The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
##
##     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

##----Create Data Frames--------
df <- data.frame(
  V1 = c(rep("a",5), rep("b",5)),
  V2 = rep(c(1:5), 2),
  V3 = c(101:110),
  stringsAsFactors = TRUE
)

match <- data.frame(
  V1 = c("a", "b"),
  V2 = c(3, 4),
  V4 = c(99,99),
  stringsAsFactors = TRUE
)



inner_join(df,match) #This has the two matching records
## Joining by: c("V1", "V2")
##   V1 V2  V3 V4
## 1  a  3 103 99
## 2  b  4 109 99
left_join(match,df)
## Joining by: c("V1", "V2")
##   V1 V2 V4  V3
## 1  a  3 99 103
## 2  b  4 99 109
df$V1<-as.character(df$V1)
inner_join(df,match) #This has only 1 record, but does not give any warning
## Joining by: c("V1", "V2")
##   V1 V2  V3 V4
## 1  a  4 104 99
left_join(match,df) #This produces the same result, Why does it match on 'a' but not on 'b'?
## Joining by: c("V1", "V2")
##   V1 V2 V4  V3
## 1  a  3 99  NA
## 2  b  4 99 104

messages.subject: Re: dplyr joins: Inconsitent behavior when matching on strings and factors
parts: This post saved me.  I was struggling to figure out why my plyr join would work but left_join would not.  I searched here for "left_join bug" and this message clued me in on my problem right away.  I had to factor one of my y columns so that it matched the corresponding x column and my problem was solved.  Thanks.
